title: History 3: Pixel by pixel, autoregressive image models

questions.q: What does the chain rule let an autoregressive image model do?
options: Write p(x) exactly as a product of p(x_i | x_1 ... x_(i−1)) over the pixels
Replace the product with an average, which is cheaper
Drop the conditioning, because the pixels of an image are independent
Sample every pixel at once, in a single network pass
questions.answer: Write p(x) exactly as a product of p(x_i | x_1 ... x_(i−1)) over the pixels
questions.why: The factorisation is exact for any order. In the lab the 64 exact conditionals multiply to the joint probability to within 9.2e-14 on 20000 images. Sampling is the part that cannot be done in one pass.

questions.q: In the lab, what happens to the derivative of output logit i with respect to input pixel j for j ≥ i in the masked network?
options: It is exactly zero, so no output sees its own pixel or any later one
It is small but not zero, about 0.07
It is zero only after training
It equals the derivative for j < i
questions.answer: It is exactly zero, so no output sees its own pixel or any later one
questions.why: The MADE masks remove every path from x_j to the prediction of x_i unless j < i. The masked network prints 0.00e+00 there, while the unmasked network prints 1.19e-01.

questions.q: Why is training an autoregressive image model fast but sampling slow, according to the PixelRNN paper?
options: Training computes all the conditionals in parallel, while generation must go pixel by pixel
Training skips the colour channels
Sampling needs a larger network than training
Training uses fewer pixels than sampling
questions.answer: Training computes all the conditionals in parallel, while generation must go pixel by pixel
questions.why: "During training and evaluation the distributions over the pixel values are computed in parallel, while the generation of an image is sequential." The lab uses 1 pass to score an image and 64 to draw one.

questions.q: In the lab the independent-pixel model gets every pixel's marginal right but costs 0.8371 bits per pixel against 0.3300 for the truth. Why?
options: It cannot see that pixels depend on each other, so it cannot know where the bar is
It was trained for fewer steps
Its marginals were wrong
It used a causal mask
questions.answer: It cannot see that pixels depend on each other, so it cannot know where the bar is
questions.why: A product of marginals ignores the dependence between pixels. Only 0.001 of its samples are well-formed bars, against 0.988 of real images.

questions.q: What reasons do the DALL·E authors give for replacing pixels with image tokens?
options: Pixels as tokens would need an inordinate amount of memory, and likelihood training spends capacity on short-range detail
Pixels cannot be fed to a transformer at all
Tokens make sampling parallel
Tokens remove the need for a causal mask
questions.answer: Pixels as tokens would need an inordinate amount of memory, and likelihood training spends capacity on short-range detail
questions.why: They compress each 256×256 RGB image to a 32×32 grid of tokens, which "reduces the context size of the transformer by a factor of 192". The lab prints 196,608 values against 1,024 tokens, ratio 192.

questions.q: What does ComfyUI's Sampler AR Video do with num_frame_per_block?
options: Denoises the latent video one block of frames at a time, each block attending to a cache of the earlier blocks
Sets how many frames the VAE decodes in parallel
Chooses how many frames are dropped from the output
Splits the prompt into one sentence per block
questions.answer: Denoises the latent video one block of frames at a time, each block attending to a cache of the earlier blocks
questions.why: sample_ar_video in comfy/k_diffusion/sampling.py loops over blocks and runs the sigma loop on each; CausalWanSelfAttention stores keys and values in a KV cache. The widget text reads "1 = framewise, 3 = chunkwise".

questions.q: You test your own masked layer and the derivative of output i with respect to input i is not zero. What does that mean?
options: The position can read itself, so the model can cheat by copying
The mask is working, because a position should see itself
The network needs more layers
Sampling will be faster
questions.answer: The position can read itself, so the model can cheat by copying
questions.why: The chain rule needs each factor to depend only on earlier elements. The lab's masked network gives exactly zero for j at or after i.
